ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-01.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-01.body:
There are $\binom42=6$ equally likely pairs. Label the balls $R_1,R_2,B,W$. The pairs containing at least one red ball are $R_1R_2$, $R_1B$, $R_1W$, $R_2B$, $R_2W$: 5 pairs (only $BW$ has no red). Exactly one of these 5 has both red, so the probability is $\frac15$.

**Answer: $\frac15$**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-02.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-02.body:
Number the rows $1$-$4$ from the top and columns $1$-$4$ from the left.

**(a)** Cut out the $2\times2$ square at the right-hand middle (rows 2-3, columns 3-4). The remaining cells split into two pieces of 6 squares: piece $P$ = all of row 1 plus the cells in row 2, columns 1-2; piece $Q$ = all of row 4 plus the cells in row 3, columns 1-2. Each is a row of four with two squares attached under (or over) its left half; they are mirror images of each other (that is why turning pieces over is allowed). Laid end to end in a $8\times2$ strip, they interlock with a $2\times2$ square: put the square at one end and fit $P$ and $Q$ together next to it, $Q$ turned over, forming the remaining $6\times2$ block.

**(b)** Cut out the central $2\times2$ square. What remains is four $1\times3$ strips arranged like a pinwheel around the centre (each strip lies along one side of the big square, starting at a corner). The four strips are congruent, and no turning over is needed. Lay them in pairs, two above two (forming two $3\times2$ blocks), on either side of the $2\times2$ square: $3+2+3=8$ wide and 2 tall.

The supervisors accept any correct $8\times2$ rectangle.

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-03.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-03.body:
They next arrive together after $\text{lcm}(18,12,14)$ minutes. $18=2\cdot3^2$, $12=2^2\cdot3$, $14=2\cdot7$, so $\text{lcm}=2^2\cdot3^2\cdot7=252$ minutes $=4$ hours $12$ minutes. $05:43+4\text{ h }12\text{ min}=09:55$.

**Answer: 09:55**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-04.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-04.body:
Think of the six triangles in a circle, with 11 as the last one. Let the others in order be $a,b,c,d,e$. The triples of adjacent triangles are $(a,b,c)$, $(b,c,d)$, $(c,d,e)$, $(d,e,11)$, $(e,11,a)$, $(11,a,b)$. Each sum must be a prime.

Since $11$ is odd and $1,3,5,7,9$ are all odd, each triple sum of three odd numbers is odd. Try the cyclic order $1,7,9,3,5,11$: triple sums are $1+7+9=17$, $7+9+3=19$, $9+3+5=17$, $3+5+11=19$, $5+11+1=17$, $11+1+7=19$, all prime. Another solution, not a reflection of the first, is the cyclic order $3,9,1,7,5,11$: sums $13,17,13,23,19,23$ (check: $3+9+1=13$, $9+1+7=17$, $1+7+5=13$, $7+5+11=23$, $5+11+3=19$, $11+3+9=23$), all prime.

A complete search gives exactly 8 solutions: the cyclic orders $1,7,9,3,5,11$; $3,9,1,7,5,11$; $3,9,7,1,5,11$; $5,1,7,9,3,11$; $5,3,9,1,7,11$; $5,3,9,7,1,11$; $5,7,1,9,3,11$; $7,1,9,3,5,11$, which form 4 pairs of mirror images. Any one, together with a second from a different pair, is correct.

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-06.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-06.body:
Put $A=(0,0)$ and $B=(7,7)$, with unit squares. Each diagonal card carries its arrow along a diagonal of a $1\times1$ square, so it moves the route by $(\pm1,\pm1)$. The long cards carry their arrow along the middle of their length, so they move the route by 1, 2 or 3 units straight. One solution is:

1. diagonal $(0,0)\to(1,1)$
2. the length-3 card $(1,1)\to(4,1)$
3. diagonal $(4,1)\to(5,2)$
4. the length-1 card turned to point upwards, $(5,2)\to(5,3)$
5. diagonal $(5,3)\to(4,4)$
6. diagonal $(4,4)\to(3,5)$
7. diagonal $(3,5)\to(4,6)$
8. the length-2 card $(4,6)\to(6,6)$
9. diagonal $(6,6)\to(7,7)$

All nine cards are used, none overlap and all lie inside the grid. (Cards are positioned so that the route is continuous, so a card may sit half a square off the grid lines.)

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-07.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-07.body:
(a) The sides satisfy $l+w=19$ and $lw=48$, so $l$ and $w$ are roots of $t^2-19t+48=0$, i.e. $(t-16)(t-3)=0$. The rectangle is $16\text{ cm}\times3\text{ cm}$.

(b) The side is $16$ cm. The area of an equilateral triangle of side $s$ is $\frac{\sqrt3}4s^2=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\times256=64\sqrt3=8^2\sqrt3$. So $a=8$ and $b=3$.

**Answer: (a) 16 cm by 3 cm, (b) $a=8$, $b=3$**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-08.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-circus-08.body:
There are three ways to split the four digits: $1+3$ digits, $2+2$ digits (and $3+1$, the same as $1+3$). For a $1$-digit by $3$-digit product, choose the single digit (4 ways) and arrange the other three in $6$ ways: 24 products. For $2$-digit by $2$-digit, the two numbers can be swapped, giving $\frac{24}{2}=12$ products. That is 36 products in total. Listing all 36 products shows that no two are equal (this is checked by working each one out), so there are $24+12=36$ different answers.

**Answer: 36**
